components.css: :host{--ground:oklch(96.6% 0.004 160);--paper:oklch(99.3% 0.002 160);--ink:oklch(21% 0.008 60);--ink-2:oklch(43% 0.01 60);--hair:oklch(85% 0.006 160);--chip:oklch(39% 0.06 50);--chip-soft:oklch(91% 0.035 80);--spring:linear(0, 0.009, 0.035 2.1%, 0.141 4.4%, 0.723 12.9%, 0.938 16.7%, 1.017 19.4%, 1.067, 1.089 24.8%, 1.084 27.6%, 1.061 30.9%, 0.996 41.1%, 0.982 46.5%, 0.985 52.6%, 1.001 71.2%, 1);--out:cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)} .ds-nav{display:flex;gap:24px;font-family:'Hanken Grotesk',system-ui,sans-serif;} .ds-nav a{position:relative;font-size:15px;font-weight:500;text-decoration:none;color:var(--ink-2);padding-block:6px;transition:color .2s} .ds-nav a::after{content:'';position:absolute;left:0;right:0;bottom:0;height:3px;background:var(--chip);transform:scaleX(0);transform-origin:left;transition:transform .5s var(--out)} .ds-nav a:hover,.ds-nav a.is-here{color:var(--ink)} .ds-nav a.is-here::after{transform:none} .ds-nav a:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--ink);outline-offset:3px}

components.name: Paint Chip
components.description: Signature: three named shades over a foot carrying the project name and the pin hole.
components.css: :host{--ground:oklch(96.6% 0.004 160);--paper:oklch(99.3% 0.002 160);--ink:oklch(21% 0.008 60);--ink-2:oklch(43% 0.01 60);--hair:oklch(85% 0.006 160);--chip:oklch(39% 0.06 50);--chip-soft:oklch(91% 0.035 80);--spring:linear(0, 0.009, 0.035 2.1%, 0.141 4.4%, 0.723 12.9%, 0.938 16.7%, 1.017 19.4%, 1.067, 1.089 24.8%, 1.084 27.6%, 1.061 30.9%, 0.996 41.1%, 0.982 46.5%, 0.985 52.6%, 1.001 71.2%, 1);--out:cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)} .ds-chip{--cw:84px;width:var(--cw);height:calc(var(--cw)*4.4);display:grid;grid-template-rows:1fr 1fr 1fr calc(var(--cw)*2.3);padding:0;border:0;border-radius:0;background:var(--paper);cursor:pointer;box-shadow:0 1px 2px oklch(20% 0.01 60 / .18),0 10px 24px -8px oklch(20% 0.01 60 / .35);transform:rotate(-6deg);transition:transform .9s var(--spring),box-shadow .4s} .ds-chip:hover{transform:rotate(0) translateY(-12px);box-shadow:0 1px 2px oklch(20% 0.01 60 / .18),0 16px 32px -8px oklch(20% 0.01 60 / .45)} .ds-chip:focus-visible{outline:2px solid var(--ink);outline-offset:2px} .ds-chip>span:not(.ds-foot){display:flex;align-items:flex-end;background:var(--s);color:var(--ink);font-family:Jost,Futura,system-ui,sans-serif;font-weight:500;font-size:11px;line-height:1.2;letter-spacing:.04em;padding:6px 7px} .ds-chip .dk{color:var(--paper)} .ds-foot{position:relative;display:flex;justify-content:center;padding:8px 0 calc(var(--cw)*.78)} .ds-foot b{writing-mode:vertical-rl;transform:rotate(180deg);font-family:Jost,Futura,system-ui,sans-serif;font-weight:500;font-size:15px;line-height:1;color:var(--ink)} .ds-foot::after{content:'';position:absolute;left:50%;bottom:calc(var(--cw)*.5 - 6px);width:12px;height:12px;margin-left:-6px;border-radius:50%;background:var(--ground);box-shadow:inset 0 1px 2px oklch(20% 0.01 60 / .35)}

components.name: Project Card
components.description: Photo, three-band strip, name and metadata on paper; no shadow.

narrative.overview:
The page is an interior designer's colour fan deck. Every project is a paint chip: a tall strip of three named shades, light to deep, with the project's name at its foot. The chip the visitor holds open decides the interface's one accent (`--chip`, the held project's deep shade, with `--chip-soft`, its light shade). Choosing a chip in the hero fan, or opening a project, sets `data-project` on the root and the primary button hover, nav underline, headline emphasis, process strip, "next palette" card, input focus, selection and brand mark all retint together. The accent belongs to whichever project is in hand, never to the studio.

Around the chips the world is quiet and mineral: a cool off-white ground, slightly brighter chip stock (paper), near-black ink, hairline rules and square corners. Colour is total inside a chip and nearly absent outside it. Type is Jost at a medium 500 with tight tracking for everything that names or labels, and Hanken Grotesk for reading. Motion is a spring: chips fan open and slide out of the deck, mini chips tilt, and the recolour crossfades over 0.6s.

The page is bilingual (Romanian default, English toggle, `?lang=en` deep link), with both languages in the markup and the root `lang` choosing which shows. It is a pitch draft: photos are labelled Pexels stand-ins, the two-bar brand mark is a provisional logo, and missing client facts show as `[de completat]` markers.
keyCharacteristics: Three named shades per project, light to deep, always shown together as a chip.
One accent, and it moves: `--chip` is the held project's deep shade.
Mineral-white ground, paper chip stock, ink, hairlines, square corners.
Jost 500 for names and labels, Hanken Grotesk 400 for reading.
Spring motion for things that are handled; soft cast shadow only on physical chips.

rules.name: The Held Chip Rule
rules.body: The interface has one accent and it is `--chip`. Never hard-code a project shade as a UI colour; read it through `--chip` / `--chip-soft` (or `color-mix` of them) so it moves when the visitor picks another project. The one exception is content that belongs to a single project (the before/after "After" tag wears wdw-petrol because the slider shows Apartament WDW).

rules.name: The Full Chroma Inside the Chip Rule
rules.body: Project shades appear at full strength only inside chips: hero fan chips, project-card strips, the dialog palette, the service mini chips, and as the photo-loading fill behind a project's own image. Outside a chip, colour reaches the page only through the held chip.

rules.name: The Three Shades Rule
rules.body: A palette is always three shades, light to deep, shown in that order with their names. Light and mid bands carry ink text; the deep band carries paper text.

rules.name: The Chip Label Rule
rules.body: Anything that names a thing (a project, a shade, a service, a step, a button) is set in Jost 500. Body copy never goes into Jost except the single about lede; nav links, hints and form labels stay in Hanken Grotesk.

rules.name: The Held Object Rule
rules.body: Only a chip, or a handle you drag, casts a shadow. If a card, panel or button needs separation, use paper on ground or a rule.

dos: Do show every palette as a chip: three named shades, light to deep, ink text on the light two and paper text on the deep one.
Do route every interface accent through `--chip` / `--chip-soft` so it follows the held project.
Do keep corners square and frame with 1px ink rules; hairlines for internal dividers; dashed rules only for what is still to come.
Do set names, labels and actions in Jost 500 with tight tracking on large sizes; read in Hanken Grotesk 400.
Do move handled things on the spring and recolour on the 0.6s out-curve; honour reduced motion.
Do ship both languages in the markup as `lang` spans and let the root `lang` pick.
donts: Don't introduce a fixed brand accent beside `--chip`; the studio's colour is whichever palette is in hand.
Don't spread project shades across sections, type or backgrounds outside a chip, except through the held chip.
Don't cast shadows from cards, panels, buttons or the header; only chips and the drag knob are objects.
Don't round corners; the pin hole is the only circle.
Don't number steps, cards or sections.
